verses.text: LORD, you’re in the right when I argue with you. Still, I want to bring you a case. Why do wicked people do so well? Why are the people who betray everyone living so comfortably?
You planted them, and they put down roots. They grow and even bear fruit. Your name is always on their lips, but their hearts are miles away from you.
But you know me, LORD. You see me and test where my heart stands with you. Drag them out like sheep headed for slaughter. Set them apart for the day they’ll be slaughtered.

How long will the land grieve and every green thing across the country dry up? The people who live there do so much evil that the animals and birds are dying off. They say, “He won’t see how things turn out for us.”
“If running with people on foot has worn you out, how are you going to race horses? You’re safe in a peaceful land, but how will you manage in the thick growth along the Jordan?
Even your own brothers and the rest of your father’s household have turned on you! Even they’ve shouted after you. Don’t believe them, no matter how sweet they sound.
“I’ve walked away from my house. I’ve cast off my inheritance. The one I love with all my heart, I’ve handed over to her enemies.
My inheritance has turned on me like a lion in the forest. She roared against me, and that’s why I’ve hated her.
Has my inheritance become a speckled bird of prey to me? Are other birds of prey closing in around her? Go gather the wild animals. Bring them in to devour her.
So many shepherds have wrecked my vineyard. They stomped all over my share of the land. They turned the place I loved into a lonely wasteland.
They left it in ruins. It cries out to me from the wreckage. The whole land’s been laid waste because nobody cares.
Destroyers have reached every bare hill in the wilderness. The LORD’s sword devours from one end of the land to the other. Nobody has any peace.
They planted wheat and harvested thorns. They wore themselves out and got nothing from it. You’ll be ashamed of what you harvest because of the LORD’s fierce anger.”

The LORD says, “As for all my wicked neighbors who lay hands on the inheritance I gave my people Israel, I’m going to pull them out of their land by the roots. I’ll pull the family of Judah out from among them too.
After I’ve pulled them up, I’ll come back and have compassion on them. I’ll bring each of them back to their own inheritance and their own land.
If they make a real effort to learn my people’s ways and swear by my name, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, they’ll be built up right among my people.
But if they refuse to listen, I’ll pull that nation up by the roots and destroy it,” says the LORD.
